sections.sectionText: Advocating and Arguing about Agriculture and the Environment: How we feed the world and manage our planet are contested issues of our time and the ability to advocate effectively and ethically about these topics is essential. Students will learn how arguments are constructed, challenged, and communicated through the exploration of rhetorical and civic perspectives. Through oral advocacy and written persuasion, students will practice defending positions, responding to competing viewpoints, and crafting evidence-based arguments on agricultural and environmental issues.

The Rhetoric of Cheese and Wine (in France!) This second 8-week course includes a mandatory study tour May TBD. More information available on the My Study Abroad Portal. There is a program fee, which includes round-trip airfare from Chicago, lodging, on the ground transportation costs, all program-related activities and most meals. Scholarships are available. Please contact the ACES Study Abroad Office at aces-studyabroad@illinois.edu for more information. Accepted students to the program will be provided permission to register for the course after February 1.

sections.sectionText: AI and Risk Communication. This course examines how artificial intelligence (AI) is influencing risk communication in agricultural and environmental contexts. Students develop a foundation in risk communication theory and apply what they learn to gain hands-on experience creating messages and strategies for different audiences, channels, and scenarios. Building on this foundation, students examine opportunities and challenges AI introduces for communication practices and decision-making. The course emphasizes critical evaluation and practical application through assignments designed to support students’ professional development. Undergraduates with instructor permission only.
